name: HIDDEN RUNG
description: Hidden Rung (or Hidden Trump) is a popular South Asian trick-taking game, part of the Court Piece (Rang) family. It is played by four players in two fixed partnerships. The game is unique for its 'hidden' trump mechanic: the trump suit is determined by a card selected from the caller's first five cards and placed face-down, remaining unknown until a player is first unable to follow suit.

content.text: Hidden Rung (or Hidden Trump) is a popular South Asian trick-taking game, part of the Court Piece (Rang) family. It is played by four players in two fixed partnerships. The game is unique for its 'hidden' trump mechanic: the trump suit is determined by a card selected from the caller's first five cards and placed face-down, remaining unknown until a player is first unable to follow suit.
Part of the Sar-Andaz or Court Piece family of games popular in the Indian subcontinent. It share roots with Whist and Bridge but features regional batch-dealing and trump-selection traditions.
4 players in fixed partnerships (North-South vs. East-West).
52-card deck and a way to track tricks (or 'Courts').

The dealer deals 5 cards to each player in the first batch. The player to the dealer's right (Trump Caller) selects their hidden trump. The remaining cards are then dealt in batches of 4 until all cards are distributed (13 per player).

items.text: Double Sir: Tricks are only picked up when a player wins two consecutive tricks.
Satat: A variant where the hidden trump card is not revealed to everyone, but the caller just announces if the played card trumps it.
